questions.question: When driving a placarded vehicle toward a railroad crossing, what should you always do?

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.explanation: When driving a placarded vehicle toward a railroad crossing, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, when should mirrors be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust all mirrors before you start driving a school bus.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts should be all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be present, free of cracks and distortions, and tight. They should show no signs of looseness, such as rust trails or shiny threads. All bolt holes must also be free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly. Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and signals at all times, follow all traffic laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.

questions.question: When inspecting engine compartment belts during the vehicle inspection test, what must you do?

options.text: Check belts for snugness, allowing up to three inches of play.
You do not need to identify the water pump belt.
Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and frays. Allow up to three-quarters of an inch of play at the center of each belt. If any of these items are not belt-driven, identify them. Make sure their components work properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.

questions.question: If you must back up a school bus at a student pick-up point, when should you do it?
questions.explanation: Backing up a school bus should be avoided whenever possible. If you must back up at a student pick-up point, wait until all students have boarded the bus first.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up students, where should students wait?

options.text: Anywhere the driver picks them up.

questions.explanation: A school bus driver should pick up and drop off students only at designated bus stops that have been approved by school district officials.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, can you exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: No, you are not permitted to stop and exit.
Yes, only if the vehicle is in reverse.
Yes, but only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, but only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, you may exit the vehicle only if you place it in neutral and set the parking brake. You may check the vehicle's position no more than twice, except during straight line backing, where you may look only once.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to perform which of these maneuvers?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: On the on-road driving test, you will be checked on how you use lanes. Which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Using the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
questions.explanation: On the on-road test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs. On roads with multiple lanes, finish turns in the correct lane. Always use or stay in the rightmost lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: When a school bus approaches a bus stop, the driver should:
questions.explanation: School bus drivers should approach stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: After finishing a basic vehicle controls skills test exercise, your vehicle must be:

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. If you do not complete an exercise exactly as described, you may lose points and could fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: If a tornado is coming and there is no shelter nearby, where should students go?
questions.explanation: If students must evacuate because a tornado is near, the driver should lead them to a building for shelter. If no building is available, the driver should take them to a nearby ditch or culvert. Avoid areas that could flood. Stay far enough away so the bus cannot fall on them if it tips.

questions.question: If you must back up at a student pick-up point, you should:

options.text: Back up before students board the bus.
Let all students board first, then back up.
Let half the students board, then back up toward the others.
Tell students to wait, then back toward the stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let all students board first, then back up.
questions.explanation: If you must back up a school bus at a pick-up point, pick up all students first. Then start backing up. Watch for students who arrive late.

questions.question: While students board and leave the bus, the driver should:

options.text: Watch the students and the loading and unloading process.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the students and the loading and unloading process.
questions.explanation: Watch students as they enter or leave the bus so they do not get caught in the door or handrails. Also make sure students move far away from the bus after they exit.

questions.question: When backing into an alley, you should first:

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: For alley backing, drive past the alley and stop parallel to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle into the alley. Park it straight and within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: On the basic control skills test, you will lose points if you:
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each mistake counts as an error against your score.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: More worn on the passenger's side.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a trailer, check that the landing gear has no missing parts and is fully raised. The crank handle should be secure and the support frame should not be damaged.

questions.question: What should the properly adjusted outside side flat mirrors on a school bus let the driver see?

options.text: The sides of the school bus
The front tires touching the ground
Vehicles in front of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides of the school bus
questions.explanation: When properly adjusted, the outside side flat mirrors should show the driver the sides of the bus, the rear tires touching the ground, and 200 feet behind the bus.
